pages.title: Surface to Underground
pages.text: Where an ordinary river enters an underground river, it no longer vanishes at the surface or leaves a one-block vertical cut. As the valley approaches the cave mouth, its ordinary river height gradually blends toward the underground entrance, leaving a readable watercourse.

pages.title: Current Behavior
pages.text: A surface opening appears only where an ordinary river truly meets an underground entrance. Mountains that merely run parallel to an underground river are not collapsed into a long V-shaped trench. Transition length follows the local river and cave blend, and only new chunks are affected.
